newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran MPs pass $2.85 bln foreign project financing.
newsitem.headline: Iran MPs pass $2.85 bln foreign project financing.

text.p: Iran's parliament on Tuesday gave the government the go-ahead to use $2.85 billion in foreign financing for major petrochemical, copper, iron and steel projects in the next Iranian year.
The financing, approved as part of the annual budget for the year starting March 21, includes $1.95 billion for projects to boost annual petrochemical output capacity by some 2.16 million tonnes.

The parliament also authorised the government to use $400 million in foreign financing to increase copper production by 100,000 tonnes and $500 million for projects to produce three million tonnes of steel and other unspecified projects.

The measure, read during parliament and broadcast live on Tehran radio, said the financing would be in the form of "buybacks", where the investor recoups his financing by receiving some of the project's output.
Before taking effect, the budget has to be approved by the clergy-based Guardian Council which vets parliamentary decisions for compatibility with Islam and the constitution.
